why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's checks and probes. The builder brief has no PASS/FAIL wording. It also reuses none of the verifier's probes: not the clean.jsonl/bad.jsonl fixture contents (`{bad`, `{"torn":` at line 5), not the `node --input-type=module -e` lint script, and not the grep or `test -f` commands. The commands it does give are allowed. Running `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` by hand comes from expect line 1, `npm ci && npm test` and the test workflow come from expect line 6, and asking the builder to write its own node:test cases is allowed. Some verifier advisories (CRLF, trailing newline, shebang/executable, package-lock) also show up in the builder brief. There they are build requirements, not probes or pass conditions, so the builder gets the bar without the checker's methods.
